doc.title: David Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 18, 2003

title: Collecting talent worldwide: Herve Samb and Cuba
summary: Berkeley-shaped open ears, the young Senegalese guitarist Herve Samb, and untapped talent in Cuba.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Berkeley man. It really is Berkeley man. I don’t have any control over that. And I think it’s just the way I grew up. I couldn’t be any other way. Right now I’m trying to hear stuff, like being in Paris, I hear all kinds of stuff. There’s a 24-year-old guitar player that’s from Senegal, his name is Herve Samb. And his mother is Vietnamese. And he’s a mixed kid. This kid, I think if there’s another Jimi, he’s going to be it. I’ve never seen anybody like that. So there’s people all over the world man, if you could see them. I just tell the guys, I says I’m going to make sure you always owe me money. Because one day they’re going to give you some. Because this kid is incredible. So he comes out on the road and he never wants to spend his money, so I always say like okay, but I always keep a tab on him. I just always want to make sure that you always owe me money. Because they’re going to give you a bunch of it one day. I hope you take care of it.
That’s good. Good to have those kind of people in your back pocket.

Yeah but I’m trying to collect these people all over the world. It’s like, it’s not in New York where you find everybody. There’s other places where you find people like, it’s one of a kind. There’s a few people like that on this planet. And I’m trying to assemble them. That’s kind of what I’m trying to do. There’s some talents down in Cuba man, that is untouched, untapped. There’s a few great people, great bands, that people haven’t even heard. Like this guy Manolito Simonet, he’s great. This guy’s got like a number two hit in Cuba. They don’t even hear about him up here.
